purpose: Public-behavior design reverse-engineering atlas for original Xziel map design. No proprietary assets, map files, scripts, source code, or extracted game data.

maps.title: Nacht der Untoten
transferableLessons: A tiny readable footprint can stay tense if every escape route has a cost.
Exterior silhouettes and blocked windows make spawn boundaries feel physical.
Minimal explanation strengthens environmental mystery.

maps.title: Verrückt
transferableLessons: Splitting players creates immediate route pressure.
A power event can transform navigation, audio, and lighting at once.
Institutional room identity makes every corridor memorable.

maps.title: Shi No Numa
transferableLessons: Hub-and-spoke layouts make route choice explicit.
Exterior weather can create fear without darkness.
Peripheral huts give each progression purchase a destination.

maps.title: Der Riese
transferableLessons: Long-term progression works best when it physically reconnects the map.
Industrial machinery can serve both lore and navigation.
Upgrade systems feel earned when tied to traversal actions.

maps.title: Kino der Toten
transferableLessons: A strong macro loop supports training while side rooms stay dangerous.
A landmark room can anchor orientation for the whole map.
Teleport return paths create controlled disorientation.

maps.title: Five
transferableLessons: Vertical transport can act as both shortcut and pressure valve.
State-change switches can reconfigure access to key systems.
Distinct floors reduce navigation ambiguity in a complex interior.

maps.title: Ascension
transferableLessons: Vehicle-like traversal nodes can double as unlock objectives.
Special rounds can attack economy rather than only health.
Large loops need interruptors so safety is never permanent.

maps.title: Call of the Dead
transferableLessons: A persistent roaming threat changes how players value safe routes.
One tall landmark can orient a sprawling map.
Environmental hazards should be readable and strategically meaningful.

maps.title: Shangri-La
transferableLessons: Compact looping geometry can feel large through elevation and one-way travel.
Environmental traps are strongest when integrated into circulation.
Claustrophobia can coexist with multiple route options.

maps.title: Moon
transferableLessons: A radically different starting state can establish identity immediately.
Environmental state changes can force route maintenance.
Movement physics can be part of map identity, not only player abilities.

maps.title: TranZit
transferableLessons: Separated combat islands can create a macro journey.
Transit should create meaningful risk, not only travel time.
Buildables can turn exploration into tangible utility.

maps.title: Nuketown Zombies
transferableLessons: Randomized progression can make a tiny map replayable.
Symmetry helps instant readability while timing uncertainty creates pressure.
Small survival maps benefit from changing resource availability.

maps.title: Die Rise
transferableLessons: Verticality must communicate irreversible drops clearly.
Moving lifts create timing-based route planning.
Traversal tools can become combat tools when placement matters.

maps.title: Mob of the Dead
transferableLessons: A secondary player state can expose hidden interactions without a separate UI.
Quest progression works when pieces live on natural traversal routes.
A strong location fantasy can unify mechanics, audio, and art.

maps.title: Buried
transferableLessons: An NPC helper can alter level geometry and economy.
Player-directed placement systems increase replayable route planning.
A maze can be tolerable when landmarks and reset behavior are consistent.

maps.title: Origins
transferableLessons: Distributed power objectives create a natural opening route.
Large maps need strong regional landmarks and recurring traversal aids.
Quest weapons are most satisfying when each path teaches the map.

maps.title: Shadows of Evil
transferableLessons: District structure scales complexity without losing orientation.
Temporary alternate interaction modes can gate traversal elegantly.
Repeating one ritual grammar across zones helps players learn a complex quest.

maps.title: Der Eisendrache
transferableLessons: Parallel upgrade routes support team role specialization.
Hazard events can temporarily revalue otherwise safe rooms.
A castle-like vertical map benefits from fast bidirectional shortcuts.

maps.title: Zetsubou No Shima
transferableLessons: Environmental systems can double as resource crafting loops.
Two-stage power gives early progression more texture.
Biological hazards make the setting itself feel hostile.

maps.title: Gorod Krovi
transferableLessons: A spectacular transport mechanic can still serve a practical fast-travel role.
Challenge stations can distribute quest pressure across the map.
Enemy ecology should match the fiction of each region.

maps.title: Revelations
transferableLessons: Disconnected themes need a consistent transport grammar.
Strong silhouettes can make surreal spaces navigable.
Reused motifs can become new gameplay when topology changes.

maps.title: The Giant
transferableLessons: Use only as evidence for how a classic layout can be modernized without changing its navigation identity.

maps.title: Voyage of Despair
transferableLessons: Long narrow maps need vertical shortcuts and room identity to avoid corridor fatigue.
Deck-based semantic naming is a strong orientation tool.
Progression can move players through a realistic structure without breaking its fiction.

maps.title: IX
transferableLessons: A central arena makes a complex map instantly legible.
Four themed spokes can teach progression through repetition.
Public spectacle can be part of atmosphere and feedback.

maps.title: Dead of the Night
transferableLessons: A mansion map benefits from strong room-purpose storytelling.
Crafting resources work best when their sources fit the fiction.
Different monster archetypes can divide pressure by space and timing.

maps.title: Ancient Evil
transferableLessons: A two-region map needs a fast, memorable transfer mechanic.
Mythic landmarks can double as progression signposts.
Parallel wonder-weapon quests support cooperative specialization.

maps.title: Blood of the Dead
transferableLessons: Shows how Mob's prison topology can be expanded and rerouted.

maps.title: Classified
transferableLessons: Shows how Five's vertical government complex can be re-authored around new progression.

maps.title: Alpha Omega
transferableLessons: Shows how a compact survival location can expand underground and gain quest layers.

maps.title: Tag der Toten
transferableLessons: Shows how a familiar coastal map can gain vertical routes and new endgame circulation.

maps.title: Die Maschine
transferableLessons: A legacy room can function as one landmark inside a much larger original route.
Parallel physical and alternate-state spaces can reuse geometry with new threat rules.
Exfil gives late-round play an optional strategic endpoint.

maps.title: Firebase Z
transferableLessons: A safe-ish village and hostile base create strong macro contrast.
Distributed reactors naturally teach the base layout.
Assault events can make perimeter defense a temporary objective.

maps.title: Mauer der Toten
transferableLessons: Dense urban verticality needs multiple fast connections.
Starting underground before reaching the street creates a satisfying reveal.
Companion systems can add utility without replacing player routing.

maps.title: Forsaken
transferableLessons: Portal-linked zones need consistent visual destination cues.
Optional side activities can create downtime between combat peaks.
A map can support both broad exploration and a directed endgame path.

maps.title: Der Anfang
transferableLessons: Objective portals convert map expansion into discrete combat missions.
A central hub supports predictable regrouping between missions.

maps.title: Terra Maledicta
transferableLessons: Open hubs need visual anchors and quick return routes.
Objective variety should change spatial behavior, not only kill targets.

maps.title: Shi No Numa Reborn
transferableLessons: Reference for modernizing a compact spoke map.

maps.title: The Archon
transferableLessons: Reference for converting an objective hub into round-based flow.

maps.title: Terminus
transferableLessons: A large island needs layered macro-navigation: foot loops locally, vehicle traversal globally.
Secure-lab interiors and exposed coastlines create strong pacing contrast.
Optional exploration should still feed back into core survival resources.

maps.title: Liberty Falls
transferableLessons: A town map becomes readable when one landmark dominates the skyline.
Broad streets need interior choke points to maintain pressure.
Compact quests can coexist with high-round training routes.

maps.title: Citadelle des Morts
transferableLessons: Castle maps should expose shortcuts as the player climbs.
Weapon-upgrade branches can map cleanly to themed subregions.
Vertical landmarks help maintain orientation through interiors.

maps.title: The Tomb
transferableLessons: Catacomb layouts need strong room silhouettes and signage to avoid visual sameness.
A supernatural subspace can act as both traversal and quest layer.
Moving utility locations create route adaptation without randomizing the whole map.

maps.title: Shattered Veil
transferableLessons: Contrasting domestic and laboratory spaces can tell the outbreak story through traversal.
Quest gates should expose new combat geometry, not only unlock rewards.

maps.title: Reckoning
transferableLessons: Tower maps need redundant vertical circulation so one route never becomes mandatory.
Floor identity should be mechanical as well as visual.
Finale spaces benefit from previewing their threat language earlier in the map.

maps.title: Ashes of the Damned
transferableLessons: A vehicle can make a very large map practical if regions remain independently readable.
Dangerous fog can turn travel itself into a gameplay phase.
Each region should support local survival before asking players to travel again.

maps.title: Astra Malorum
transferableLessons: A singular scientific landmark can unify cosmic fiction and navigation.
Elite enemies should force route changes rather than simply add health.

maps.title: Paradox Junction
transferableLessons: Time-state variants are most legible when the base footprint remains recognizable.
State changes can alter resource placement and route value without rebuilding the whole map.
Temporal travel needs explicit before/after landmarks.

maps.title: Totenreich
transferableLessons: Weather and coastal exposure can make exterior lanes feel dangerous even when wide.
Ancient settlement plus hidden lab creates a natural surface/subsurface reveal.
A lighthouse is an excellent global orientation anchor.

maps.title: Kowakujō
transferableLessons: A hazard landscape should shape route choices, not merely decorate edges.
Castle tiers work best with readable ascent goals.
Folklore-inspired elites can reinforce regional identity.

maps.title: Rex Infernus
transferableLessons: Finale maps benefit from compressing learned systems into a high-pressure route.
Boss mechanics should echo environmental hazards seen before the arena.

maps.title: Outbreak
transferableLessons: Mobility unlocks can transform the same geometry mid-match.
Area-specific power creates localized progression.
Open zombie entry points change defensive behavior compared with repairable windows.

maps.title: Infection
transferableLessons: Temporary contamination can turn safe routes into emergencies.
Objective civilians create movement pressure during survival rounds.

maps.title: Carrier
transferableLessons: Objective interruptions can force teams to abandon preferred loops.
Ship decks naturally support layered routing and chokepoints.

maps.title: Descent
transferableLessons: A contained facility can escalate through repeated boss pressure without changing the whole map.
Underwater fiction can justify hard boundaries and emergency systems.

maps.title: Zombies in Spaceland
transferableLessons: Theme-park districts are a strong way to give each spoke unique mechanics.
Minigames can create optional downtime without leaving the map.
Traps are memorable when they are physically tied to attractions.

maps.title: Rave in the Redwoods
transferableLessons: Alternate visual states can reinterpret a familiar route.
Forest maps need landmark lighting to prevent navigation collapse.

maps.title: Shaolin Shuffle
transferableLessons: Player combat-state progression can coexist with map progression.
Dense cities need district identity and vertical shortcuts.

maps.title: Attack of the Radioactive Thing
transferableLessons: A deliberately readable town can support unusually complex puzzles.
Environmental hazards should have obvious fiction and activation language.

maps.title: The Beast from Beyond
transferableLessons: Cross-mode enemy reuse works when encounter roles are re-authored for the map.
Endgame-heavy maps need a stable early-game economy first.

maps.title: The Final Reich
transferableLessons: Guided objectives can coexist with secrets if the critical path stays diegetic.
A surface village plus buried facility creates natural horror escalation.
Body-horror enemies are stronger when foreshadowed by environment.

maps.title: The Darkest Shore
transferableLessons: Dynamic fog can periodically rewrite sightline strategy.
Island maps should preserve multiple return routes to the core.
Environmental bombardment can make exterior timing matter.

maps.title: The Shadowed Throne
transferableLessons: Dense ruined cities need strong interior/exterior rhythm.
Enemy mutations can be triggered by map systems to create emergent risk.

maps.title: The Tortured Path
transferableLessons: Short maps can form a campaign when progression state carries across stages.
Objectives should force distinct movement patterns per stage.

maps.title: The Frozen Dawn
transferableLessons: Descending deeper is a strong physical metaphor for escalating horror.
Weapon quests can map cleanly to four themed trials.
Multi-level subterranean spaces need aggressive landmarking.

maps.title: Gröesten Haus
transferableLessons: Reference for extremely small survival footprints and resource scarcity.

maps.title: Urzikstan Zombies
transferableLessons: Use only as reference for macro-region threat zoning and extraction, not classic round-based pacing.
